topic: Open‑source LLM inference on AWS Trainium with TrnRT
sourceTitle: Show HN: TrnRT – An open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium
postText:
Trainium is finally getting the open-source LLM love it deserves

- The new TrnRT engine shows you can run GPT-style models on Trainium with latency under 30 ms per token, beating many GPU setups on cost per token.

- Because it’s built on the same AWS Neuron SDK, integration with SageMaker or EKS is a few CLI commands, meaning you don’t need a dedicated ML ops team to spin up inference.

- The open-source nature means you can tweak the kernel for your own model size, and the repo already includes scripts to benchmark on a single Trainium chip vs a p4d.24xlarge GPU - the results are eye-opening for workloads under 2 B parameters.

- For startups, the pricing model of Trainium (pay-as-you-go with no upfront hardware) turns what used to be a $10k GPU cluster into a few cents per hour, making experimental LLM services financially viable.

- The community around TrnRT is already contributing optimizations for mixed-precision inference and adding support for emerging tokenizers, which signals a fast-moving ecosystem that could keep Trainium relevant even as newer chips arrive.
